title: Rewrite the message queue with delivery guarantees
description: Pick at-least-once or exactly-once and justify the choice. Implementation must include the broker, one producer, one consumer, and a failure-injection test.

title: Estimate-at-the-whiteboard practice
description: Run three estimation questions verbally. Record. Self-review.

title: Read 'Designing Data-Intensive Applications' Chapter 7
description: Transactions chapter. Come with one question per section. We discuss in session.

title: Write the 'happy week in 5 years' paragraph
description: One paragraph, honest, no filter. We'll revisit it in month three.

title: Paper prototype: first ten seconds of a hiking game
description: Use only paper. Three sketches minimum. The first-ten-seconds question is the design problem.

title: GPS noise filtering for the hiking-trail Flutter app
description: Pick a simple filter (moving average or Kalman). Implement, measure error before/after, write a paragraph on the trade-offs.

title: Draft research statement v1 → v3
description: Three full drafts in the first two weeks. Different opening, different framing each time.

title: Read three papers from each target advisor
description: Use the abstracts to filter; full read on the most-cited. Take notes on the question they're asking, not just the result.

title: Build a sustainable writing routine
description: 60 minutes a day, same time. Two weeks consecutive. Report at our next session whether it stuck.

title: Multi-stage Docker build + measurement
description: Take an existing service, write a multi-stage Dockerfile, measure image size and cold start before/after.

title: VPC + IAM hands-on labs
description: Two weeks of lab work in your free AWS account. Peering, transit gateway, IAM policy debugging. No more reading without doing.

title: Build and operate a small platform
description: ECS service + CloudWatch metrics + a documented runbook for one failure mode. Ship it; document it.

title: Read 20 audit reports
description: Mainstream firms only. Note the pattern of finding categories. Stop CTFs for the month.

title: Write three formal bug reports
description: One per month for months 2-4. Real findings or simulated; the writing is the skill.

title: OSCP exam preparation block
description: Structured prep, lab time, mock exam at week 8. Real exam scheduled for month four.

title: Apply to five security internships
description: Targeted applications, not spam. One paragraph per company on why this team.

title: ADR #1: Pagination strategy for the feed
description: Write your own architecture decision record before reading mine. Include trade-offs, alternatives considered, and the test the decision needs to survive.

title: ADR #2: Caching strategy
description: Same exercise. Decide between memory-only, persisted, and hybrid. Justify with concrete failure modes.

title: State management refactor + ADR
description: End-to-end refactor of the state-management layer in your app. Write the ADR first, then ship the code.

title: Cross-team meeting facilitation prep
description: Prepare to run a 30-minute cross-team meeting in our org (I'll provide the topic). Agenda, decisions list, and a written follow-up. We rehearse before.

title: Architecture interview prep — 4 mock interviews
description: Four mock architecture interviews over four weeks. I'll run them in interview format with feedback.

title: Rewrite cover letter — no apology paragraph
description: Cut every sentence that explains 'why you're not a developer.' Keep only what you bring.

title: Five companies actually wanted, not five hiring
description: Real shortlist. One paragraph per company on why this team specifically.

title: Portfolio: three real content audits
description: Audit a small business's existing content, write a one-page improvement memo for each.

title: Wrap document: lessons from the engagement
description: One page of lessons we both write down, signed by both.

title: Daily research journal, weeks 1-4
description: One entry per day, minimum 200 words, written immediately after reading. No retroactive entries. Send weekly summary.

title: Close read of three foundational interpretability papers
description: Choose three: one classic (>5 years old), one modern, one disputed. Write a one-page reading note for each.

title: Draft 'research vs industry' decision memo
description: Two-page memo arguing the case for each path, with explicit weights on the factors. Final session reviews this.

title: Drive Sakarya–Düzce, 6 honest discovery calls
description: Cold walk-ins at logistics warehouses. Notebook only; no slides.

title: Write the startup's obituary (3 pages)
description: If this fails, why? Three pages, before the next call.

title: Cofounder search: three serious conversations
description: Identify three people you'd actually want as cofounder. Have the conversation. Report back.

title: Decision call and wrap document
description: Write the wrap doc together. Be specific about what you learned.

title: Customer discovery: 6 cold conversations
description: Find a problem worth a startup, talk to six potential customers cold. Notebook only.

title: Pre-mortem: 3 pages on why the startup would fail
description: Be honest about the dominant failure mode. The dominant one is the answer.
